dedupe_keys.name: planned relocation of a municipal campsite and floodplain restoration in the saane valley pacco normandy france

description: This Climate-ADAPT case study describes managed retreat in the lower Saâne valley in Normandy, France, one of two pilot sites of the cross-border Interreg project PACCo (Promoting Adaptation to Changing Coasts, 2020 to 2023), the other being the Lower Otter valley in Devon, UK. Facing river and coastal flooding, erosion and sea level rise, the municipal campsite at Quiberville was moved out of the floodplain, a new sewage treatment plant was built, and land was bought to restore about 50 hectares of wetland and reconnect the river to the sea, with restoration due by 2026. The municipality spent nearly 500,000 euro on land for the new campsite, the Caux Terroir community of communes 100,000 euro on the treatment plant, and the national coastal protection agency over 2 million euro on land. It sits within Normandy's Notre Littoral Pour Demain programme (from 2014) and a 25 million euro fund from ERDF and the region. The page is free HTML on the Climate-ADAPT portal (2024). Caveats: relocation strains local budgets, outcomes of restoration are still to come, and figures are project reported. It illustrates adaptation planning by relocating municipal infrastructure and restoring floodplains; a related record is the Global NbS opportunity areas dataset.
name: Planned relocation of a municipal campsite and floodplain restoration in the Saâne valley (PACCo, Normandy, France)
notes: Conservatoire du littoral is taken as the national coastal protection agency named on the page.
outcomes: A campsite and wastewater plant were moved out of the floodplain and about 50 ha of wetland land bought for restoration, at a combined cost of over 2.6 million euro.
